title: Sales Commission Calculator
prompt:
Calculate commission using multiple sales thresholds.

Skills: Logical functions and nested conditions.

Use the supplied synthetic CSV at assets/data/practical-09-sales-commission-calculator.csv. A small copy/pastable sample is included below in case the CSV is not directly downloadable from the lesson page. Complete the work in a separate .xlsx copy, preserve a raw-data sheet, and check the result against the acceptance criteria. Then answer the short grading check; it does not validate the workbook itself.

Sample CSV (synthetic):
SalesRep,Sales,CommissionRate
Riya,18000,0
Kabir,32000,0
Mira,54000,0
objective: Calculate commission using multiple sales thresholds.

starter.instructions: Open/import the UTF-8 CSV into Excel. Keep the original source data unchanged and perform work on a separate sheet or workbook.

expected_output: Expected: rates are applied at the documented threshold, including values just below, at, and above each boundary.

public_tests.name: Sample-data acceptance
checklist: Input records are preserved and data types are checked.
Totals/results reconcile with a small independent calculation.
An edge case, duplicate or threshold boundary is tested where relevant.

public_tests.name: Server-side answer check
public_tests.note: A text/choice check does not execute Excel or inspect the workbook artifact.

acceptance_criteria: Expected: rates are applied at the documented threshold, including values just below, at, and above each boundary.
Use a labeled result area and document formulas, assumptions or transformation steps.
Compare actual results with a manual/independently calculated expected result and test one edge case.
Keep source data intact and request human review of the completed workbook; do not treat the text grader as artifact validation.
hints: Import data without losing dates, decimals or leading zeros.
Separate raw inputs, calculations and presentation outputs.
Test empty inputs, duplicated keys, boundary values or missing matches as appropriate to the scenario.
grading_method: Server-side exact_text check of the submitted answer/expression only; does not execute Excel or inspect the workbook. This workbook-practice task needs a human-reviewed artifact and test evidence for full acceptance. Illustrative threshold example only: under 30,000 = 5%, from 30,000 to below 50,000 = 7%, and 50,000 or more = 10%. Those rates are teaching assumptions, not taken from the PDF.
retry_policy: Retries are permitted. A failed string/choice submission does not complete the exercise. Course files do not define XP; platform-wide server logic applies.
